QF.id: XVI Clearing, Settlement and Risk Management_62

question.text: In commodity futures, what type of margin is the seller exempted from when a warehouse receipt is provided as proof of holding the commodity?

answer.text: Tender period/delivery period margin — the seller is exempted

explanation.text: The Logic: When delivery intention exists and the seller provides proof of holding the commodity through a valid warehouse receipt, the seller is exempted from the tender/delivery period margin because the delivery risk is already mitigated by demonstrated physical holding. The Trap: Initial margin, Extreme Loss Margin and Mark-to-Market margin are not affected by warehouse receipts. Only the delivery-period margin is exempted in this scenario. Note: Distributor/cross-exam coaching labels removed; stem reworded to say the seller is "exempted from" rather than simply "released" from the margin.
